$comment: THE declared generation targets. Each entry is one obligation the generator discharges for EVERY Ω Nucleus, the template that renders it, and the destination it lands at. This document — not any module — is the answer to 'what does generating a nucleus produce'. Adding an artifact to every future nucleus is an entry here and requires NO change to generator.py, registry.py or contracts.py; supplying a different renderer for an existing obligation is a template registration and requires no change either.
$destination_comment: Destinations are patterns over tokens the DECLARATION can answer — {contracts_path}, {errors_path}, {bootstrap_path}, {cli_path}, {registry_path}, {catalog_path}, {package_path}, {slug}. This is why the generator holds no repository knowledge: the contract artifact lands wherever the nucleus says its contract surface lives, not wherever a convention would have put it. A pattern naming a token the declaration cannot answer is refused at plan time, never guessed. A project whose layout differs supplies its own targets document; the set below is the packaged default, not a law.

targets.rationale: The register entry through which the nucleus enters constitutional authority. Rendered in the register document's own shape so it is directly registrable — the Repository Truth update the generation produces, offered as a determination rather than applied as a side effect.
UFC-01 and UFC-08. A consumer binds to a named, semantically versioned contract; a nucleus with no published contract is not a nucleus.
UFC-10. Every absence is a typed refusal carrying a distinct stable code, so the nucleus can never substitute an inference for a determination it cannot make.
UFC-03 and UFC-05 together: the population is held deterministically and fail-closed, and new authority enters it by registration rather than by editing the nucleus that consumes it.
UFC-02 and UFC-07. One declared path into existence, no import-time side effect, and a service descriptor that makes the nucleus resolvable rather than merely importable.
UFC-06. A nucleus that can only be exercised from a test or an interactive session cannot be operated.
UFC-04. Behaviour is configured by a declared document that resolves and parses. Configuration that lives in code cannot be changed without a release, which means it is not configuration.
Documentation derived from the declaration cannot drift from it. This is the only kind of documentation the Foundation is willing to be responsible for.
The executable obligations that arrive with the artifact. A generated artifact with no obligation attached is a claim, not a capability.

UFC-06 again, from the build's side: a declared entry point the build does not publish is a runtime surface nobody can reach. Rendered as a fragment because merging it into the build manifest is a constituent act, not a generation side effect.
